text:
maya: Heads-up — running into weird mypy errors in the Python SDK async client when using autogenerated pydantic models and the auth/retry layer. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

jon: saw something similar last week. can you paste the stack and a small repro?

maya: repro below — minimal async call + generated model types. mypy complains about 'Incompatible return type' on the client method even though runtime works.

maya: ```py
# generated_models.py (autogen)
from typing import Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Choice(BaseModel):
    text: str

class CompletionResponse(BaseModel):
    choices: Optional[list[Choice]]

# client.py (async)
async def create_completion(prompt: str) -> CompletionResponse:
    resp = await httpx_async.post("https://api/redwood/v1/generate", json={"prompt": prompt})
    return CompletionResponse.parse_obj(resp.json())
```

maya: mypy error: `error: Incompatible return value type (got "CompletionResponse | None", expected "CompletionResponse")` — but the method never returns None at runtime.

jon: that looks like the autogenerated typing uses Optional for list[Choice], but mypy sometimes widens pydantic model unions when parse_obj returns Union[Model, None] for nullable root. do you have --strict?

eric: another angle — sync client stubs were generated with `-> CompletionResponse`, async client stubs get `-> Optional[CompletionResponse]` because of a quirk in the codegen that tried to represent a 204/empty-body case. so the emitted type differs between sync/async.

sam: confirmed — codegen branch "unify-return-typing" exists but only applied to the sync templates. bug.

maya: ugh. also noticed auth/retry behavior discrepancy: sync client auto-retries on 401 once after refreshing creds, async client just bubbles the 401. related?

eric: probably related to differences in the transport wrapper. sync client uses requests + a small retry shim that calls auth.refresh() and retries. async client uses httpx.AsyncClient but we didn't wire the same retry hook for coroutine paths.

jon: quick workaround: in your code, cast the return `cast(CompletionResponse, ...)` or assert not None, but obviously not ideal for users.

sam: plan: (1) fix codegen templates so sync+async emit identical return types, (2) add shared retry hook for httpx async transport that mirrors sync behavior, (3) add mypy+pyright check in CI to catch regressions.

maya: that would be great. can we prioritize the codegen template change first? it's low-risk and will reduce noise for customers using typing checks.

eric: I'll open a PR today for codegen template parity. tagged it DRAFT and added a unit test. linking in thread: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/912 :eyes:

jon: for async auth retry I can sketch an adapter that injects an auth hook into AsyncClient event hooks — should be straightforward. will add tests that simulate a 401 then refresh.

sam: CI note: when we ran the branch tests, ci-bot reported one flaky test in auth/test_retry_async.py — flaky due to timing. we're going to make that deterministic by mocking httpx transport.

ci-bot: ci/pipeline #4702 failed on auth/test_retry_async.py (timeout). rerun queued.

maya: awesome — thanks all. if PRs land I'll smoke-test with my project and report back. :thumbsup:

eric: thanks — will ping when draft is ready for review.

jon: moving to fix the async retry adapter now.

sam: adding a small devex doc note to the onboarding guide about "mypy quirks with generated models" until the fix ships.

maya: cool — appreciate it.
